artiest/grateful-dead.text:
Grateful Dead came into being in 1965 in Palo Alto, near San Francisco. The band grew out of a jug band and a bluegrass group around the guitarist Jerry Garcia, who also played banjo. At first the group was called The Warlocks. Garcia found the new name by opening a dictionary. The permanent core consisted of Garcia, the guitarist Bob Weir, the bassist Phil Lesh, the drummer Bill Kreutzmann and the keyboard player Ron 'Pigpen' McKernan, later joined by the drummer Mickey Hart. Robert Hunter wrote many of the lyrics. The band was the house band of the writer Ken Kesey's Acid Tests, happenings at which LSD played a large part, and so belonged to the heart of the hippie movement.

The first records, such as Anthem of the Sun (1968) and Aoxomoxoa (1969), were psychedelic and experimental, but sold poorly. The live album Live/Dead (1969), with long improvisations such as Dark Star, gave a better idea of what the band did on stage. In 1970 they surprised everyone with Workingman's Dead and American Beauty, with short, acoustic songs full of country and folk. Not until 1987 did they have their only top 40 hit, Touch of Grey.

Grateful Dead's music blends rock, blues, jazz, folk, country, bluegrass and gospel. Their strength lay in the concerts, where they improvised at length and freely and no two evenings sounded the same. Fans, the Deadheads, were allowed to record the concerts and traded the tapes among themselves. In this way the group remained one of America's top-earning live acts for decades and is regarded as the progenitor of the jam bands. After Garcia's death in 1995 the band stopped.
artiest/grateful-dead.listen: Listen to Dark Star on the live album Live/Dead and notice how the musicians start to improvise from a simple theme. Compare that with one of the short, acoustic songs of Workingman's Dead or American Beauty.

artiest/green-day.text:
Green Day was founded in 1987 in Rodeo, California, by the singer and guitarist Billie Joe Armstrong and the bassist Mike Dirnt. The band was first called Sweet Children and in 1989 chose the name Green Day. In 1990 the drummer Tré Cool joined, succeeding John Kiffmeyer. The group grew up in the punk scene around the club 924 Gilman Street in Berkeley and released its first records on the small label Lookout! Records.

The breakthrough came with Dookie (1994), the first album on the major label Reprise. The producer Rob Cavallo recorded it with the band at Fantasy Studios in Berkeley. The sound was punk, short and fast, but with melodies you could sing along to after one hearing. Basket Case, in which Armstrong writes about his panic attacks, spent five weeks at number 1 on the American alternative radio chart and reached number seven in England. At Woodstock '94 the performance ended in a mud fight with the audience. In 1995 Dookie won a Grammy for Best Alternative Album.

After grunge, Green Day made punk suitable for the hit parade again, and pop punk became a genre of its own. In 2004 came American Idiot, a narrative album about America after 9/11, which won a Grammy for Best Rock Album. In 2010 it premiered on Broadway as a musical. In 2015 the band was inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame in the first year it was eligible.
artiest/green-day.listen: Basket Case begins with only Billie Joe Armstrong's voice and guitar; then the band comes in. Listen to the chord sequence in the verse: the same progression as in Pachelbel's Canon, but at punk tempo.

artiest/gregory-coleman.text:
Gregory C. Coleman was an American drummer who played with The Winstons, a funk and soul group from Washington, D.C. He died on 5 February 2006 at the age of 61. Coleman played drums and sang backing vocals. His name is linked to a single recording: Amen, Brother, the B-side of the 1969 single with Color Him Father on the A-side.

Halfway through Amen, Brother there is a drum solo, played by Coleman. That solo became the breakbeat known as the Amen break, and made the single the most sampled record in history. The A-side, Color Him Father, was a success: the record sold more than a million copies, was certified gold on 24 July 1969 and won a Grammy for Best R&B Song of 1970. The song reached number seven on the Billboard Hot 100.

The group, whose members came from different backgrounds, had trouble getting gigs in the South and broke up in 1970. Coleman's short solo had a long life. Hip hop producers and, later, drum and bass producers cut the bars out of the song and used them again and again. In this way a few seconds of drumming determined the rhythms of an entire genre.
artiest/gregory-coleman.listen: Listen to Amen, Brother by The Winstons and notice the drum solo halfway through. Hear how short and dry the drums sound, and try to imagine how something like that is used again and again as a loop.

artiest/groep-1850.text:
Groep 1850, also called Group 1850, was a Dutch psychedelic rock band founded in 1964 in The Hague. The group was first called Klits and in 1966 was renamed Groep 1850, when the first single, Misty Night and Look Around, appeared on the small label Yep. Few copies were pressed, but the record made them known as one of the most original Dutch bands, alongside The Outsiders and Q65. The group then signed with Philips.

On Philips came more singles in a strongly psychedelic style, including I Know, Mother No-Head, which reached number twenty-four in the Netherlands in 1967, Zero and We Love Life. In 1968 and 1969 the albums Agemo's Trip to Mother Earth and Paradise Now appeared. Shortly afterwards the band split up, but it was active now and then in the 1970s. Releases included the album Polyandri and, in 1971, the single Fire with Have You Ever Heard? on Polydor.

Outside the Netherlands the group never had success, but today it is regarded as one of the most innovative acid rock bands of its time. S.I.X., Sjardin's Terrible Surprise and Orange Upstairs later emerged from the same milieu. Groep 1850 shows that the psychedelia of the 1960s had an adventurous side of its own in the Netherlands too.
artiest/groep-1850.listen: Listen to Mother No-Head (1967) and notice the guitars and the vocals, which unfold like a dreamlike, slightly menacing trip. Hear how far this sounds from the ordinary hit parade of the time.

artiest/grover-washington-jr.text: The saxophonist Grover Washington Jr. grew up in Buffalo and later lived in Philadelphia. In the early 1970s he made soul-jazz records with funk grooves for the label Kudu, a division of CTI. Mister Magic (1975) was a great success. On Winelight (1980) is Just the Two of Us, sung by Bill Withers, a worldwide hit. His warm, singing tone on soprano and tenor saxophone became the model for a whole generation of smooth jazz saxophonists, among them Kenny G. He died in 1999, shortly after a television appearance.
artiest/grover-washington-jr.listen: Listen to the saxophone that sings like a soul singer.

artiest/gucci-mane.text:
Gucci Mane, real name Radric Delantic Davis, is an American rapper and music entrepreneur, born on 12 February 1980 in Bessemer, Alabama. At the age of nine he moved with his mother to Atlanta. He began rapping at fourteen. After his first CD, La Flare, which circulated in East Atlanta in an edition of about a thousand copies, he joined the label Big Cat Records.

In 2005 his debut album Trap House appeared, with the single Icy featuring Young Jeezy. The album did well for an independent release. Together with the Atlanta rappers T.I. and Jeezy he is regarded as one of the makers who brought trap music to a large audience in the 2000s. He kept releasing mixtapes and collaborations and signed with Warner Bros. Records. His sixth album The State vs. Radric Davis (2009) was his commercial breakthrough, with the double platinum single Lemonade, and reached the top ten of the Billboard 200.

Gucci Mane has released sixteen studio albums and seventy-one mixtapes since 2001. In 2007 he founded the label 1017 Records, which signed Young Thug, Waka Flocka Flame, Chief Keef and Pooh Shiesty, among others. He has worked with The Weeknd, Drake and Mariah Carey, among others. His great influence lies in the way he gave trap and new talent a platform.
artiest/gucci-mane.listen: Listen to Lemonade and notice the slow, heavy beat and the loose, almost lazy-sounding way in which he raps. Hear how the chorus sticks in your head.

artiest/guided-by-voices.text:
Guided by Voices is an American indie rock band, founded in 1983 in Dayton, Ohio. The only constant through all the line-ups is the singer and writer Robert Pollard. The best-known line-up consisted of Pollard, his brother Jim, Mitch Mitchell, Tobin Sprout and Kevin Fennell. The group began as a pub band and increasingly became a studio project. The first records were self-financed and released independently.

Their first recognition outside the city came in 1992 with Propeller, of which only five hundred copies were pressed, each with its own hand-made sleeve. Bee Thousand followed in 1994 and is regarded as a milestone of indie rock. It was released through Scat Records, with distribution by Matador Records. In 1995 came Alien Lanes, largely assembled from fragments recorded at home, for the most part on a four-track recorder. Later the group signed with larger labels, and albums such as Isolation Drills made the Billboard top two hundred. In 2004 Pollard disbanded the band, in 2010 the classic line-up returned, and since 2016 the group has been going again.

The influences lie in early British beat music, garage rock, psychedelia, prog rock, punk and post-punk. The band has released forty-three albums and gained a loyal following. Guided by Voices is regarded as a key name in lo-fi music, in which short, sloppily recorded songs are precisely the strength.
artiest/guided-by-voices.listen: Listen to a track from Bee Thousand and notice the rough recording with hiss and short, almost sketch-like songs. Hear how a beautiful melody survives despite the poor sound.

artiest/guido-van-arezzo.text:
Guido of Arezzo was an Italian music theorist and teacher of the High Middle Ages, born around the year 991 or 992. He was a Benedictine monk and is regarded as the inventor, or according to some the developer, of the modern musical staff, which had a great influence on Western music notation. Little is known about his life. Most of what we know comes from two letters: a dedicatory letter to Bishop Tedald of Arezzo and a letter to his colleague Michael of Pomposa. His birthplace is uncertain. The two candidates are Arezzo in Tuscany and the abbey of Pomposa on the Adriatic coast.

Around 1013 he went to the abbey of Pomposa, one of the most famous Benedictine monasteries of his time, to complete his training. There he developed the principles of the staff, an ordered visual system for writing and reading music. He set them down in his antiphonary, with a prologue in which he wrote that singers spent far too much time learning melodies by heart. His new teaching method brought him the irritation of his colleagues.

Bishop Tedald later asked him to train the singers of Arezzo cathedral. There he wrote the Micrologus, a handbook for singers, dedicated to the bishop. Without his staff, music could not be read in the way we know today, not even in pop music.
artiest/guido-van-arezzo.listen: Look at a page of sheet music while you play a song and follow the lines with your eye. Notice how notes written higher or lower also sound higher or lower, the principle that Guido set down.

artiest/guillaume-de-machaut.text: Guillaume de Machaut was a poet and composer, served as secretary to King John of Bohemia and became a canon of Reims cathedral. He had his work collected in costly manuscripts, as a result of which more of his work has survived than that of any contemporary. His Messe de Nostre Dame, from the early 1360s, is the oldest complete polyphonic mass by a single composer. He also wrote love songs in fixed forms such as the ballade, rondeau and virelai.
artiest/guillaume-de-machaut.listen: Listen to the Kyrie and hear how four voices make raw, open sonorities that sound very different from later harmony.

artiest/guillaume-dufay.text: Guillaume Dufay began as a choirboy in Cambrai and later returned there as a canon. In between he worked for years in Italy and Savoy, including in the papal chapel. He added the soft sound of English thirds and sixths to the French tradition and made the mass into one coherent whole. His motet Nuper rosarum flores was heard in 1436 at the consecration of Florence cathedral, beneath Brunelleschi's new dome.
artiest/guillaume-dufay.listen: Listen to Nuper rosarum flores and notice how the high voices sing freely above two low voices that very slowly carry a plainchant melody.

artiest/gulzar.text:
Gulzar, born Sampooran Singh Kalra on 18 August 1934, is an Indian Urdu poet, lyricist, writer, screenwriter and film director from Hindi cinema. He was born into a Sikh family in Dina, in what is now Pakistan. At school he read translations of Tagore, which was a turning point for him. With the Partition of the country his family was torn apart, he had to break off his studies and came to Mumbai.

His career as a lyricist began in 1963 with the film Bandini, with the composer S.D. Burman. He worked under the directors Bimal Roy and Hrishikesh Mukherjee, and wrote the lyrics of Aashirwad (1968). He had a close bond with the composer Rahul Dev Burman and also worked with Salil Chowdhury, with Madan Mohan on Mausam, and later with Vishal Bhardwaj. As a director he made his debut in 1971 with Mere Apne, followed by Aandhi, Mausam and Maachis, among others, films about human relationships in a social context. He often uses flashbacks in his stories.

He has won five Indian National Film Awards, twenty-two Filmfare Awards, an Oscar and a Grammy, among others. In 2004 he also received the Padma Bhushan. He writes in Urdu and Punjabi, in the Triveni stanza, and wrote ghazals for Jagjit Singh. His poetic lyrics gave film songs a literary layer.
artiest/gulzar.listen: Listen to a song from the film Mausam or Aandhi with lyrics by Gulzar and pay attention to the words. Hear how a simple image evokes a feeling in a few lines.

artiest/gundula-janowitz.text:
Gundula Janowitz is an Austrian lyric soprano, born on 2 August 1937 in Berlin. She grew up in Graz, where she attended the conservatory and became an Austrian citizen. As early as the late 1950s she sang at the highest level, in 1960 in Haydn's Die Schöpfung with Herbert von Karajan. In 1959 Karajan engaged her as Barbarina in Mozart's Le nozze di Figaro in Vienna. In the 1960s and 1970s she was one of the most popular singers in the world.

Her discography runs from Bach to Richard Strauss. She worked with conductors such as Karajan, Otto Klemperer, Eugen Jochum, Leonard Bernstein, Rafael Kubelík, Karl Böhm, Georg Solti and Carlos Kleiber. Well-known recordings are Die Zauberflöte under Klemperer, Carmina Burana under Jochum, Der Freischütz under Kleiber, and under Karajan the St Matthew Passion, the Mass in B minor and Strauss's Vier letzte Lieder, among others. She appeared at Glyndebourne, Bayreuth, the Metropolitan Opera, the Opéra de Paris, La Scala and Covent Garden, among others. In 1990 she took her leave of the opera stage as Ariadne auf Naxos, and until 1997 she still gave song recitals.

Her voice is known for a pure, creamy sound and a fast vibrato. She mastered above all the high and middle registers and lyrical, emotional expression. Janowitz is regarded as one of the most famous opera singers of the twentieth century.
artiest/gundula-janowitz.listen: Listen to Janowitz in Richard Strauss's Vier letzte Lieder and notice the pure, smooth tone with which she sings the long lines. Hear how her voice floats effortlessly above the orchestra.

artiest/guns-n-roses.text:
Guns N' Roses is an American hard rock band from Los Angeles, founded in March 1985 by Axl Rose, Izzy Stradlin and Tracii Guns, among others, who came from the groups L.A. Guns and Hollywood Rose. Their two names were combined into the band's name. After initial changes, the classic line-up was settled in June 1985, with the singer Rose and the guitarist Slash. Later members included the bassist Duff McKagan. The band broke through with the album Appetite for Destruction (1987), which includes Sweet Child O' Mine. The mini-album G N' R Lies followed in 1988.

In 1991 the albums Use Your Illusion I and Use Your Illusion II appeared, after which a long world tour followed, with incidents such as the Riverport Riot in 1991. Stradlin left during that tour and was replaced by Gilby Clarke, who played on the covers album The Spaghetti Incident? (1993). Chinese Democracy appeared in 2008. After years of open feuding, Slash and McKagan rejoined the band in 2016 for the Not in This Lifetime... Tour, which earned 563.3 million dollars. Guns N' Roses is one of the best-selling groups of all time.

The early sound united the rawness of punk with the loud guitars of hard rock and heavy metal. Slash plays famous guitar lines, Rose has a shrill, high voice, and the band sings about the raw side of life in Los Angeles. In the late 1980s Guns N' Roses brought danger back into hard rock, at a time when pop and glossy metal dominated the charts.
artiest/guns-n-roses.listen: Listen to Sweet Child O' Mine and first follow the guitar line that opens the song. Then notice how the vocals become higher and rawer and how the band lets rip at full force at the end.

artiest/gunter-lenz.text:
Günter Lenz was a German jazz bassist and composer, born on 25 July 1938 in Frankfurt am Main and died on 26 June 2026. He first taught himself to play guitar and then studied with Carlo Bohländer. From 1954 he played jazz in the clubs of the American army. During his military service in 1959 and 1960 he switched to the bass. In 1961 Albert Mangelsdorff brought him into his quintet.

Lenz also played in the jazz ensemble of the broadcaster Hessischer Rundfunk, for which he arranged and composed. In 1965 he played in Krzysztof Komeda's quintet on the album Astigmatic. In the 1970s he was in Kurt Edelhagen's big band and worked in Munich with Jerry van Rooyen and Peter Herbolzheimer. Chet Baker, Coleman Hawkins, Oliver Nelson and Benny Bailey took him on tour and into the studio. In the middle of that decade he played in the avant-garde band Clarinet Contrast and in Manfred Schoof's quintet.

At the end of the 1970s he started his own group Springtime, playing international jazz fusion, and recorded albums such as Beyond and Where the Hammer Hangs. He also wrote orchestral arrangements for Plácido Domingo. From 2001 to 2006 he was a professor at the Musikhochschule Stuttgart, and in 2004 he received the Hessian jazz prize.
artiest/gunter-lenz.listen: Listen to the album Astigmatic by Krzysztof Komeda and notice the bass that fills the space beneath the horns. Hear how Lenz supports the music calmly and precisely.

artiest/gunther-schuller.text:
Gunther Schuller was an American composer, conductor, horn player, writer, historian, teacher, publisher and jazz musician. He was born on 22 November 1925 in Queens, New York, to German parents. His father Arthur was a violinist with the New York Philharmonic. He studied at the Saint Thomas Choir School and became an excellent horn player and flautist. At fifteen he was already playing professionally, with the American Ballet Theatre, and in 1943 he became principal horn of the Cincinnati Symphony Orchestra. He then played in the Metropolitan Opera orchestra in New York until 1959. He never earned a diploma. He died on 21 June 2015.

Schuller made a career in jazz by recording as a horn player, and released records such as Music for Brass in 1957 and Modern Jazz Concert in 1958. Later he wrote works such as The Red Back Book (1973), Piano Concerto (1986) and Mass in D (1992). His piece Transformation (1957) is an example of the fusion of jazz and modern classical music, a direction he called Third Stream.

Schuller connected, worldwide, two musical worlds that rarely came together: the improvisation of jazz and the tight compositional techniques of modern classical music. As a teacher and historian he also wrote about jazz. For anyone who listens to pop music he is important as an advocate of the idea that genres can enrich one another.
artiest/gunther-schuller.listen: Listen to Transformation and try to hear where the piece sounds like a chamber orchestra and where the improvisation of the jazz musicians takes over. Can you hear the boundary, or do they merge into one another?

artiest/gurrumul.text:
Geoffrey Gurrumul Yunupingu, Gurrumul for short, was an Aboriginal musician of the Yolŋu people in Australia. He was born on 22 January 1971 and died on 25 July 2017. After his death he was also called Dr G. Yunupingu. He was born blind in Galiwin'ku on Elcho Island, off the coast of Arnhem Land in northern Australia, well over five hundred kilometres east of Darwin. He was the eldest of four sons. He played several instruments: drums, keyboards, guitar, a right-handed strung guitar that he played with his left hand, and didgeridoo.

His solo debut Gurrumul appeared in 2008, with the song Wiyathul. Rrakala followed in 2011, The Gospel Album in 2015 and, posthumously, Djarimirri: Child of the Rainbow in 2018. In 2021 the compilation The Gurrumul Story appeared.

Gurrumul sang mainly in languages of his people. His voice was soft and clear, and was accompanied by acoustic guitar and few other instruments, so that his songs sound almost like prayers. He brought the singing and the stories of the Yolŋu to a large audience in Australia and beyond, and is one of the best-known Aboriginal artists. His work shows how a deeply personal voice can turn an age-old tradition into pop music.
artiest/gurrumul.listen: Listen to Wiyathul and notice how soft and clear his voice sounds above the acoustic guitar. How many instruments do you actually hear, and what space does the music leave open?

artiest/guru.text:
Guru, in full Keith Edward Elam, was an American rapper, producer and actor, born on 17 July 1961 in Roxbury, a district of Boston. He died on 19 April 2010, at the age of forty-eight, of multiple myeloma. His father Harry Justin Elam Sr. was a lawyer and judge, and the first African American judge to be appointed to the Boston Municipal Court. Elam began under the name MC Keithy E and later changed it to Guru. In 1987 he founded Gang Starr, with DJ Premier. The first records, produced by The 45 King on Wild Pitch Records, attracted little attention. After a change in the line-up the group did break through.

Alongside Gang Starr, Guru began the Jazzmatazz series, of which Volume 1 appeared in 1993 with Loungin'. Volume II followed in 1995, Volume 3 in 2000 and Volume 4 in 2007. He also made solo albums such as Baldhead Slick & Da Click (2001) and Version 7.0 (2005). In 2012 About.com placed him at number 49 of its top 50 MCs, and The Source called his lyrics particularly thoughtful.

Guru's voice is low, calm and dry, and he talks more than he shouts. In Jazzmatazz he combined hip hop with live jazz musicians, which made him one of the pioneers of jazz-rap fusion. His style proved that a rapper could also sound relaxed and thoughtful, and the combination of jazz and beats was later taken up by many others.
artiest/guru.listen: Listen to Loungin' and notice how Guru's calm, almost spoken rap fits the jazz sounds of the accompaniment. Can you hear how relaxed the rhythm stays?

artiest/gustav-mahler.text: Gustav Mahler was above all a conductor, for ten years among other things director of the Vienna Court Opera, and composed in the summers. He wanted a symphony to embrace a whole world and let folk songs, marches, sounds of nature and large choirs exist side by side. The Adagietto from his Fifth Symphony, for strings and harp, is regarded as a declaration of love to his wife Alma. Willem Mengelberg made the Concertgebouw Orchestra an early champion of his music.
artiest/gustav-mahler.listen: Listen to the Adagietto and hear how only strings and harp play, with a melody that keeps putting off where it wants to go.

artiest/gustavo-santaolalla.text: Gustavo Santaolalla (born in 1951 in Argentina) began in the 1960s with the rock group Arco Iris and later became an influential producer of rock en español. His film work began with Alejandro González Iñárritu's Amores perros (2000). His music is sparse: a few notes on guitar or on the ronroco, a small Andean stringed instrument, with plenty of space and silence. For Brokeback Mountain (2005) and Babel (2006) he won an Oscar two years running. For the game The Last of Us (2013) he used the same bare, acoustic sound, and that also took him to the television series. He proves that few notes can carry a great deal of emotion.
artiest/gustavo-santaolalla.listen: Listen to the acoustic guitar or ronroco, the long silences between the phrases and the reverb that makes the instrument sound lonely.

artiest/guus-meeuwis.text:
Guus Meeuwis was born in 1972 in the monastery of Mariahout, a Brabant village where his parents were living temporarily. He grew up in neighbouring Lieshout and studied law in Tilburg. After a romantic weekend in Bruges with his girlfriend he wrote the song Het is een nacht. With his student band he won the first student song contest in Leiden with it in 1994. A talent scout offered the group a record contract. The band continued as Guus Meeuwis & Vagant, named after their regular pub.

In 1995 Het is een nacht went to number 1 in the Dutch Top 40, and a year later Per spoor did the same. Hits such as Zo ver weg and Ik wil met je lachen followed. In 2001 Vagant split up, and from 2002 Meeuwis continued solo, with his brother Marc and the pianist Jan-Willem Rozenboom still in his band. His first solo album included Brabant, which was soon called the unofficial anthem of the province. More than 30,000 people even signed a petition to make it the official anthem. In 2015 he was the first Dutch-language artist to give a sold-out concert at the Royal Albert Hall in London.

Meeuwis sings Dutch-language songs about love, friendship and home, with simple melodies that are easy to sing along to. As a result his performances became great parties where the audience sings every word. In 2013 he was made a Knight of the Order of Orange-Nassau.
artiest/guus-meeuwis.listen: Listen to Brabant and pay attention to the chorus. Hear how simple the melody is and how the song is made to be sung along to by a large group of people.

artiest/guy.text:
Guy is an American R&B group founded in 1987 by Teddy Riley, Aaron Hall and Timmy Gatling. Riley and Gatling grew up in Harlem in New York, in households where a great deal of music was made, inspired by groups of the late 1970s such as the Gap Band, Earth, Wind & Fire and the Jacksons. They played from an early age in local bands for audiences aged twelve to twenty. After the first album Damion Hall, Aaron's younger brother, took Gatling's place.

The debut album Guy appeared in 1988, sold more than a million copies and went double platinum. It includes Groove Me. The Future followed in 1990 and Guy III in 2000. Guy is regarded as the pioneer of new jack swing, a style that was worked out and popularised by Riley.

New jack swing combines the singing of soul and R&B with the hard rhythms and samples of hip hop. The drum machine is up front, the singing is full and soulful, and the beat is tight and danceable. Guy showed that in the late 1980s soul could sound like the street and the club, and Teddy Riley would go on, as a producer, to shape that style for others too. The group belongs to the roots of what later became mainstream R&B.
artiest/guy.listen: Listen to Groove Me and notice the hard, mechanical drum machine and the warm, soulful singing on top of it. Can you hear how those two worlds complement each other?

artiest/guy-manuel-de-homem-christo.text:
Guy-Manuel de Homem-Christo is a French musician, producer and composer, born on 8 February 1974 in Neuilly-sur-Seine. He is best known as one half of the French electronic duo Daft Punk, together with Thomas Bangalter. His parents ran an advertising agency in Paris, and on Sundays his father played rock records by Led Zeppelin and the Eagles. As a child he was given a toy guitar, and at fourteen an electric guitar, which he still uses when writing music.

In 1987 he met Bangalter at the Lycée Carnot in Paris, where the two discovered their love of films and music from the 1960s and 1970s. Together with Laurent Brancowitz they first formed the indie rock band Darlin'. Daft Punk made Discovery (2001), Human After All (2005), the soundtrack of TRON: Legacy (2010) and Random Access Memories (2013), among others. With The Weeknd they made Starboy in 2016, their first number one on the Billboard Hot 100. In 2021 the duo announced its end.

Outside Daft Punk he founded the label Crydamoure with Bangalter and made music with Le Knight Club. He produced Sexuality by Sébastien Tellier, and later co-wrote songs for Charlotte Gainsbourg and Travis Scott. He himself prefers to stay out of the limelight. In this way he belongs to the producers who brought dance music and pop closer together.
artiest/guy-manuel-de-homem-christo.listen: Listen to Starboy by The Weeknd and Daft Punk and notice the tight electronic beat and the vocoder voice. Hear how the sound of Daft Punk fits into a pop song there.

artiest/gwen-foster.text:
Gwen Foster, also spelled Gwin or Gwyn, was born in 1903 in Caldwell County, North Carolina. He played harmonica and guitar in old-time music, the rural folk music of the Appalachians that later became one of the roots of country. He worked in the textile mills. There he met the banjo player Dock Walsh, with whom he formed a band. Foster played in groups such as The Carolina Tar Heels and the Blue Ridge Mountain Entertainers.

He owes his place in pop history mainly to a single recording. On 6 September 1933 Foster and Clarence Ashley recorded the song Rising Sun Blues for the label Vocalion. It is the oldest known recording of the song that later became known as The House of the Rising Sun. The song had lived on as a folk song for some time, and in the decades that followed it would be sung by many artists, until in 1964 it became a worldwide hit in the version by The Animals. In this way the recording by Ashley and Foster links the old folk music of the mountains with the pop music of the 1960s. Gwen Foster died in 1954 in Dallas, North Carolina.
artiest/gwen-foster.listen: Listen to Rising Sun Blues by Clarence Ashley & Gwen Foster (1933) and then to The House of the Rising Sun by The Animals. Notice what stays the same, such as the story, and what changes in tempo, instruments and singing.

artiest/gyorgy-ligeti.text: György Ligeti grew up as a Hungarian Jew in Transylvania, survived the war and fled to the West in 1956. In Cologne he got to know the electronic studio, and after that he wrote orchestral works made up of dense, slowly shifting textures of sound. Atmosphères (1961) has no melody or metre to follow, only colours that flow into one another. Stanley Kubrick used it, together with Lux aeterna, in 2001: A Space Odyssey.
artiest/gyorgy-ligeti.listen: Listen to Atmosphères and hear how an enormous sound without melody or rhythm slowly changes colour, as if you are moving through clouds.

artiest/haddaway.text:
Haddaway's full name is Nestor Alexander Haddaway, and he was born in 1965 in Trinidad and Tobago. His father was a marine biologist, his mother a nurse. After his parents' divorce he grew up in America, first in Chicago and from the age of nine in the Washington area. Louis Armstrong inspired him to take up the trumpet at fourteen, and at high school he played in the school band. In 1987 he left for Cologne, where he worked in pubs and started a company of his own for fashion shows. There he wanted to build a career in music and dance.

In 1992 he signed with the German label Coconut Records. His first single, What Is Love, became an enormous hit in Europe in 1993. The song reached number 1 in thirteen countries, including the Netherlands, and was also a hit in America. Life, I Miss You and Rock My Heart also reached the top ten in Europe. His second album, The Drive (1995), included the hit Fly Away. After that his success waned. What Is Love later got a second life through sketches on Saturday Night Live, the film A Night at the Roxbury and remixes.

Haddaway was one of the most successful Eurodance artists of the 1990s. Eurodance was fast, electronic dance music from Europe, with a solid beat, synthesizers and a singer with a powerful chorus. With What Is Love he delivered one of the best-known songs of that style.
artiest/haddaway.listen: Listen to What Is Love and notice how a Eurodance track is built: a fast, straight beat, bright synthesizer chords and a chorus with a question that keeps coming back. Hear how Haddaway's powerful voice carries the song.

artiest/hailu-mergia.text:
Hailu Mergia is an Ethiopian keyboard player, accordionist, composer and arranger who now lives in Washington, D.C. He was born in 1946 in Debre Birhan and at the age of ten moved to Addis Ababa. He grew up with traditional Amharic melodies and taught himself to play the accordion at fourteen. He left school and joined the music department of the army, where he learned to read and write music. He then became a freelance musician in the nightclubs of Ethiopia, until in the Zula Club he met the future members of the Walias Band.

In the 1970s he was the keyboard player of the Walias Band, a jazz and funk group with a hard, polyrhythmic funk sound, influenced by Western musicians such as King Curtis, Junior Walker and Maceo Parker. Under the rule of the Derg, censorship was a problem. Hailu often chose instrumental music, because singers had to support the government. From the Walias Band, Tche Belew appeared in 1977, one of only three instrumental albums from the golden years of Addis Ababa. He emigrated to the United States and in 1985 recorded his album Shemonmuanaye entirely on his own. Later he worked as a taxi driver at Dulles Airport and wrote music in his car. In 2013 and 2016 his old records were reissued, and in 2018 came Lala Belu, his first new album in more than thirty years.

Hailu Mergia turns folk melodies into funkier, modern music. His keyboard playing and accordion have a warm, swinging sound. He is a key figure of the Ethiopian golden age and an example of how forgotten records find a new audience after decades.
artiest/hailu-mergia.listen: Listen to Tizita and follow the keyboards, which make the melody sound like a singing voice. Notice the melancholy tone and how softly the accompaniment stays underneath.

artiest/hal-blaine.text:
Hal Blaine was born in 1929 as Harold Belsky in Holyoke, Massachusetts, the child of Jewish immigrants from Eastern Europe. He began drumming at the age of eight. His father worked in a nightclub, and Hal went along to watch the drummers of the jazz bands and orchestras. As a boy he survived the great Hartford circus fire of 1944, where he had gone mainly to see the drummer of the circus band. That same year the family moved to California.

After drum lessons with Roy Knapp, who had also taught Gene Krupa, he played night after night in clubs in Chicago, where he quickly learned to sight-read. He played in Count Basie's big band and then went into the studio. Unlike many jazz musicians, he enjoyed playing rock 'n' roll. In the 1960s he was the regular drummer of the group of session musicians in Los Angeles that he himself called The Wrecking Crew. He played on records by Phil Spector, The Beach Boys, Simon & Garfunkel, Frank Sinatra, Elvis Presley, The Byrds and The Carpenters. His beat on Be My Baby by The Ronettes (1963) came about by accident: he hit the snare drum only on the fourth beat, and Spector let that mistake stand.

Blaine played, by his own estimate, on more than 35,000 recordings, including 150 American top 10 hits. He gave the hits of the 1960s their rhythmic foundation, while the public hardly knew his name. In the 1980s the work declined because of drum machines. In 2000 he was inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame. He died in 2019.
artiest/hal-blaine.listen: Listen to the beginning of Be My Baby by The Ronettes. Notice the drum intro: a heavy bass drum and then one hard hit on the snare drum, on the fourth beat. Hear how that simple pattern carries the whole song.

artiest/hal-david.text:
Hal David was an American lyricist, born on 25 May 1921 in New York and died on 1 September 2012. His parents were Austrian-Jewish immigrants who ran a delicatessen, and his older brother Mack David was also a lyricist. He studied journalism. In the 1940s he wrote lyrics for bandleaders such as Sammy Kaye and Guy Lombardo. In 1956 he began working at the Brill Building in New York with the composer Burt Bacharach, for the publishing company Famous Music.

In the 1960s and the early 1970s the duo wrote a series of songs that have endured, many of them for Dionne Warwick, but also for Dusty Springfield, Carpenters, B.J. Thomas, Gene Pitney and Tom Jones. Their hits include Alfie, Walk On By, I Say a Little Prayer, Do You Know the Way to San Jose, This Guy's in Love with You and What the World Needs Now Is Love. For Raindrops Keep Fallin' on My Head from the film Butch Cassidy and the Sundance Kid they received an Oscar. They also made the musical Promises, Promises (1968). Their collaboration ended after the disappointing film Lost Horizon (1973).

David also wrote with other composers, such as To All the Girls I've Loved Before with Albert Hammond and We Have All the Time in the World with John Barry, which Louis Armstrong sang for a James Bond film. His lyrics are simple, direct and full of feeling, and have been decisive for the sound of 1960s pop music.
artiest/hal-david.listen: Listen to Walk On By by Dionne Warwick and notice how the lyrics describe a painful moment in ordinary words. Hear how Bacharach's music gives each line a colour of its own.

artiest/halle-orchestra.text:
The Hallé, or Hallé Orchestra, is an English symphony orchestra from Manchester. The pianist and conductor Charles Hallé put it together in May 1857 for the Manchester Art Treasures Exhibition. He then decided to continue the orchestra as a permanent organisation, and on 30 January 1858 it gave its first concert. Its first home was the Free Trade Hall. In 1861 the orchestra was in financial difficulties and gave only two concerts that year.

In 1888 the German violinist Willy Hess became leader. Hans Richter was music director from 1899 to 1911, and in his time the orchestra gave the first performance of Edward Elgar's First Symphony. In 1943 the orchestra had shrunk to thirty players. Sir John Barbirolli, who led it until 1970, brought it back to national level. Kent Nagano was principal conductor from 1992 to 1999. In 1996 the orchestra moved to the Bridgewater Hall in Manchester, where it still plays.

The records of the 1950s and 1960s reveal the broad repertoire, from Mozart's Jupiter Symphony to Ravel's La Valse, Debussy's La Mer, Sibelius's Finlandia and songs by Mahler. The Hallé shows how a city orchestra outside London can build a musical life of its own.
artiest/halle-orchestra.listen: Listen to Sibelius's Finlandia played by the Hallé and notice how the brass make the opening sound heavy and menacing. Hear how the strings later take over the broad, calm melody.

artiest/hamid-el-kasri.text:
Hamid El Kasri is a Moroccan gnawa musician, born in 1961 in Ksar El Kebir and now living in Rabat. He is regarded as a maâlem, a master of the tradition. His surname is a stage name that simply means: from Ksar El Kebir. He began his training at the age of seven. Gnawa is the spiritual music of Morocco, played on the guembri, a three-stringed bass lute, and on large metal castanets, with call-and-response singing and a repeating, trance-like rhythm.

He became known outside Morocco and regularly plays with foreign musicians, often at the Gnaoua World Music Festival. In 2004 he performed there with Joe Zawinul, in 2010 with Karim Ziad and in 2011 with Hamayun Kahn and Shahin Shahida. In 2018 he opened the festival with the jazz group Snarky Puppy. That year he also played with Jacob Collier at the BBC Proms and was heard on Collier's album Djesse Vol. 1, on the song Everlasting Motion. His own albums include Bouhala Gnawa (2007), Yobadi (2016), Salam (2020) and Roots & Plugged (2022), which features Moulay Ahmed.

El Kasri shows how an age-old spiritual tradition can combine with jazz and world music. The tight, repeating rhythms of gnawa suit improvisation well, and as a result he has become a bridge between Morocco and the international stage.
artiest/hamid-el-kasri.listen: Listen to Moulay Ahmed and follow the low, round sound of the guembri. Notice how the singing and the choir's response come in above the repeating rhythm.

artiest/hamlet-gonashvili.text:
Hamlet Gonashvili was a Georgian tenor, influential teacher and interpreter of Georgian folk music. He was born on 20 June 1928 in eastern Georgia and died on 25 July 1985. He was sometimes called the Voice of Georgia. He is regarded as the finest interpreter of songs from the regions of Kartli and Kakheti, and received many national honours and prizes.

Gonashvili devoted himself to the traditional singing of Georgia, which is known for its polyphony. His 1983 album bears a title in Georgian and contains folk songs. Hamlet appeared in 1995, also posthumously. Tsintskaro, the piece from the course, belongs to the traditional repertoire. The Georgian composer Giya Kancheli drew inspiration from Gonashvili's singing for his Third Symphony, and Gonashvili himself was the soloist at the first performance of that work.

Georgian folk singing is polyphonic, with long, harmonic lines and often a low drone beneath the melody. Gonashvili sang with a powerful, clear tenor voice and many graceful ornaments. He shows how old and developed the singing traditions of the Caucasus are, long before pop music experimented with harmonies. His voice is one of the best known in Georgian music.
artiest/hamlet-gonashvili.listen: Listen to Tsintskaro and notice the ornaments in Gonashvili's voice. Can you hear how the long notes move slowly, and how the accompanying voices or instruments lay a bed beneath the melody?

artiest/han-bennink.text: The drummer Han Bennink from Zaandam began as a young drummer in swing and bebop; Kenny Clarke was his model. He accompanied American soloists visiting the Netherlands, such as Eric Dolphy in 1964 and Sonny Rollins in 1967. He then became one of the best-known free improvisers in Europe. In 1967 he founded the Instant Composers Pool with Misha Mengelberg and Willem Breuker, and he played for years with Peter Brötzmann. Bennink plays on anything that makes a sound: his drum kit, the floor, chairs, the stage. His performances are energetic and funny. He is also a visual artist.
artiest/han-bennink.listen: Hear how swing and free sound alternate in the drums.

artiest/hank-jones.text:
Hank Jones, in full Henry Jones Jr., was an American jazz pianist, bandleader, arranger and composer, born on 31 July 1918 in Vicksburg, Mississippi and died on 16 May 2010. He grew up in Pontiac, Michigan, in a musical and religious family of ten children. His father thought that playing jazz was the work of the devil. Even so, Jones was influenced by pianists such as Earl Hines, Fats Waller, Art Tatum and Teddy Wilson. At thirteen he was already playing in Michigan and Ohio.

In 1944 the saxophonist Lucky Thompson brought him to New York, where he got to know bebop and worked with Coleman Hawkins and Billy Eckstine, among others. In 1947 he went on tour with Jazz at the Philharmonic, and from 1948 to 1953 he was Ella Fitzgerald's accompanist. He also played with Artie Shaw, Benny Goodman, Lester Young and Wes Montgomery, and on Cannonball Adderley's Somethin' Else with Miles Davis. From 1959 to 1975 he was a staff pianist at CBS. On 19 May 1962 he accompanied Marilyn Monroe when she sang Happy Birthday, Mr. President.

Jones recorded more than sixty albums under his own name and played on some thousand recordings. Critics call his playing eloquent, lyrical and impeccable. In 1989 he received the NEA Jazz Masters Award. He shows how a pianist with taste and gentleness can support a singer or soloist.
artiest/hank-jones.listen: Listen to Somethin' Else by Cannonball Adderley and notice the piano, which softly and precisely fills the space beneath the horns. Hear how Jones never does more than necessary.

artiest/hank-marvin.text:
Hank Marvin was actually called Brian Rankin and was born in 1941 in Newcastle upon Tyne. He first played banjo and piano, but after hearing Buddy Holly he chose the guitar. He even adopted Holly's spectacle frames. His stage name combined his nickname Hank with the first name of the country singer Marvin Rainwater. In 1958, at the age of sixteen, he went to London with his schoolfriend Bruce Welch. At the 2i's Coffee Bar in Soho, Cliff Richard's manager asked him to be a guitarist. Marvin said yes, if Welch could come too.

Cliff Richard's backing band was first called The Drifters, but had to choose another name in 1959 and became The Shadows. Besides their work with Richard, the group became famous in its own right with instrumentals such as Apache (1960), F.B.I. (1961), Wonderful Land (1962) and Foot Tapper (1963). Marvin also wrote songs for Richard and for the group. From 1969 he also made solo records; on the first, his guitar plays against an orchestral accompaniment. Since 1986 he has lived in Australia.

In 1959 Cliff Richard bought him a red Fender Stratocaster, probably the first in England. With that guitar and an echo unit Marvin found his own clear sound. He plays the melody the way a singer sings, with great feeling in every note. He was regarded as the first British guitar hero and defined the role of the lead guitarist. Many later guitarists, such as George Harrison, Eric Clapton, Brian May, Mark Knopfler and Neil Young, name him as a model.
artiest/hank-marvin.listen: Listen to Apache by The Shadows and notice Hank Marvin's guitar, which plays the melody like a singer. Hear the echo on the guitar and the clear tone of his Stratocaster.

artiest/hank-mobley.text:
Hank Mobley was an American jazz tenor saxophonist and composer, born on 7 July 1930 in Eastman, Georgia and raised in Elizabeth, New Jersey, near Newark. As a child he played piano. When he was sixteen and stuck at home ill for months, his grandmother bought him a saxophone. He was refused entry to a music school in Newark because he did not live there, and taught himself theory and harmony from books.

At nineteen he played in local bands, and soon afterwards he worked for the first time with Dizzy Gillespie and Max Roach. Roach introduced him to the New York jazz world in 1951. He then often played with the drummer Art Blakey, in one of the first hard bop sessions, together with Horace Silver, Doug Watkins and Kenny Dorham. In the second half of the 1950s he recorded a great deal for Blue Note, with Lee Morgan, Donald Byrd, Art Farmer, Jackie McLean and Herbie Hancock, among others. In the 1960s he worked mainly as a leader and recorded for Blue Note until 1970. Soul Station (1960) is regarded as his best record, and Roll Call also dates from that year.

The critic Leonard Feather called him the middleweight champion of the tenor saxophone. His tone was not as fierce as John Coltrane's and not as soft as Lester Young's. He died on 30 May 1986. He shows how hard bop can also be relaxed and melodic.
artiest/hank-mobley.listen: Listen to Soul Station (1960) and notice the round, warm tone of the tenor saxophone. Hear how he plays with loose, melodic phrases rather than with lots of notes.

artiest/hank-shocklee.text:
Around Hank Shocklee arose The Bomb Squad, the production team behind the hip hop group Public Enemy. The team included Keith Shocklee, Eric Sadler and Chuck D, the rapper of Public Enemy, who contributed under the name Carl Ryder. From the debut Yo! Bum Rush the Show (1987), The Bomb Squad made the music for the group. It Takes a Nation of Millions to Hold Us Back (1988), the single Fight the Power (1989) for the film Do the Right Thing and Fear of a Black Planet (1990) followed.

The productions of The Bomb Squad were dense and full. In a single track they sometimes used dozens of samples, and they deliberately sought out harsh, grating sounds that were not neatly in tune. In this way a wall of sound arose that sounded as restless and urgent as Chuck D's political lyrics. The team also worked for other artists, such as Ice Cube on AmeriKKKa's Most Wanted (1990), Slick Rick, LL Cool J and Bell Biv DeVoe, and made remixes for Sinéad O'Connor, Peter Gabriel and Janet Jackson, among others.

The working method of Shocklee and his team showed that a sampler could be an instrument for building a new sound of one's own. They stacked fragments from old records into something that no longer resembled the sources. The Bomb Squad is counted among the most important hip hop producers.
artiest/hank-shocklee.listen: Listen to Fight the Power or a track from It Takes a Nation of Millions to Hold Us Back by Public Enemy. Try to pull the layers apart: how many different samples, scratches and other sounds do you hear at once beneath the raps?

artiest/hank-thompson.text:
Hank Thompson, in full Henry William Thompson, was an American country singer and songwriter. He was born on 3 September 1925 in Waco, Texas and was active for seven decades until his death on 6 November 2007. As a child he played harmonica in competitions. After his service in the navy in the Second World War as a radio operator and a course in electrical engineering at Princeton, he decided to go into music.

His first number one came in 1952 with The Wild Side of Life, with the line about honky tonk angels. That line inspired an answer song, It Wasn't God Who Made Honky Tonk Angels, which became the first hit for Kitty Wells. From 1947 to 1964 he recorded for Capitol Records, and later for Warner Bros., Dot and MCA. Albums include Songs for Rounders and Smoky the Bar.

His style is called honky tonk western swing, with fiddle, electric guitar and steel guitar and his smooth baritone voice. His backing band, the Brazos Valley Boys, was voted best country band by Billboard fourteen years in a row. He brought a light version of Bob Wills's western swing, with the emphasis on the danceable beat. Thompson was inducted into the Country Music Hall of Fame in 1989. The 1987 novel Crazy Heart is based on his life, and was filmed in 2009.
artiest/hank-thompson.listen: Listen to The Wild Side of Life and notice the fiddle and the steel guitar that carry the melody. Hear how the soft baritone voice lets the line about the honky tonk angels fall calmly.

artiest/hank-williams.text:
Hank Williams was born in 1923 as Hiram Williams in Mount Olive, a rural community in Alabama. His mother played organ in the Baptist church, and the hymns there later coloured his own songs. He got guitar lessons from Rufus Payne, a black street musician who played blues and taught him how important rhythm and timing are. He also listened to country singers such as Roy Acuff. Williams never learned to read music. He wrote from stories and from his own experiences.

At the end of the 1930s he was already singing on the radio in Montgomery, with his band The Drifting Cowboys. In 1947 came the hit Move It On Over, and he appeared on the radio programme Louisiana Hayride. In 1949 followed his version of Lovesick Blues, an older song that went to the top of the country chart and won him a place at the Grand Ole Opry. He then wrote Your Cheatin' Heart, Hey, Good Lookin' and I'm So Lonesome I Could Cry. His songs are simple in form, with a plaintive, nasal voice and lyrics about love, loneliness and drink.

Williams had back pain all his life and became addicted to alcohol and painkillers. On New Year's Day 1953 he died, aged 29, on the back seat of a car, on his way to a concert. Even so, he became one of the most influential musicians of the twentieth century. Chuck Berry, Elvis Presley, Johnny Cash, Bob Dylan and The Rolling Stones learned from him, and his work helped country grow into a major force in American culture.
artiest/hank-williams.listen: Listen to Lovesick Blues and notice how, on the long notes, Hank Williams lets his voice break into a high falsetto, almost like a yodel. Hear too how the steel guitar answers his singing.

artiest/hanns-eisler.text: Hanns Eisler was born in Leipzig in 1898 and grew up in Vienna, where he studied with Arnold Schönberg. In Berlin he worked with Bertolt Brecht and wrote protest songs for the workers' movement. For the film Kuhle Wampe (1932) he composed the 'Solidaritätslied'. In 1933 he fled from the Nazis. In America, with the support of the Rockefeller Foundation, he investigated how music and film go together, including with Joris Ivens's short film Regen. With Theodor Adorno he wrote the book Composing for the Films, a fierce critique of Hollywood habits. For Fritz Lang he wrote Hangmen Also Die! (1943). In 1948 he was expelled from the US. For Alain Resnais he composed Nuit et brouillard (1956).
artiest/hanns-eisler.listen: Notice how the music does not weep along with the image but keeps its distance from it: cool, clear sounds accompanying horrifying images make the viewer think.

artiest/hannu-lintu.text:
Hannu Lintu is a Finnish conductor, born on 13 October 1967 in Rauma. His father was an electrical engineer and his mother a photographer. He studied piano and cello at the Turku conservatory and at the Sibelius Academy, and received conducting lessons from Atso Almila and later from Jorma Panula and Eri Klas.

From 1998 to 2001 he was principal conductor of the Turku Philharmonic Orchestra, and from 2002 to 2005 of the Helsingborg Symphony Orchestra in Sweden. From 2009 to 2013 he led the Tampere Philharmonic Orchestra. In 2013 he became the eighth principal conductor of the Finnish Radio Symphony Orchestra, and he remained so until the end of the 2020 to 2021 season. After that, from 2021 to 2026, he was chief conductor of the Finnish National Opera and Ballet. Outside Finland he was principal guest conductor of the RTÉ National Symphony Orchestra in Ireland. Since 2023 he has been principal conductor of the Gulbenkian Orchestra in Lisbon, and from 2026 he is music director of the Singapore Symphony Orchestra.

Lintu has recorded for labels such as Claves, Dacapo, Danacord, Hyperion, Naxos and Ondine. His recordings show that he conducts both classical and modern repertoire.
artiest/hannu-lintu.listen: Listen to a recording under Lintu and notice how the orchestra builds from soft to loud. Hear how the conductor guards the balance between the strings and the winds.

artiest/hans-dulfer.text: The tenor saxophonist Hans Dulfer from Amsterdam has been playing a raw mixture of jazz, funk and soul since the 1960s. On his records he constantly sought new combinations, including with Latin musicians and punk musicians. He is one of the best-known figures of the Amsterdam jazz scene and still performs, regularly with his daughter Candy Dulfer. He likes the contrast between jazz and pop music, and likes to seek out audiences outside the jazz clubs. His tone is big and loud, with plenty of blues and a touch of humour.
artiest/hans-dulfer.listen: Notice the raw, loud tone of the tenor sax.

artiest/hans-erdmann.text:
Hans Erdmann was a German composer, born on 7 November 1882 and died on 21 November 1942. He wrote music for a number of German films at a time when film was still silent and the music was played live by an orchestra in the auditorium. His name remains linked above all to a single title: Nosferatu (1922), the vampire film for which he composed the score.

After Nosferatu, Erdmann continued to work for film. His other well-known film music includes Le testament du Dr. Mabuse, the 1933 film also known under the title The Testament of Dr. Mabuse, and Augustus the Strong (1936). It is work for the image: music that carries the tension of a scene and gives a film a tone colour of its own, even before spoken dialogue existed.

For pop history Erdmann is a forerunner in the background. He belongs to the first generation of composers who asked themselves what music accompanying moving images should do. Anyone who understands the later film music in De Droomfabriek (The Dream Factory) will see here where that tradition begins. In 1995 an edition of his Nosferatu score appeared under the title Nosferatu: A Symphony of Horror.
artiest/hans-erdmann.listen: Listen to an excerpt from the Nosferatu music on Nosferatu: A Symphony of Horror. Notice how the music builds menace without a single word, and what you imagine when you cannot see the images.
